dedupe_keys.name: japan 5th mesh 250 m hazard summary and population exposure dataset

description: This dataset combines hydro-meteorological and tsunami hazard information with population exposure on Japan's standard 5th-level grid, the roughly 250-metre mesh, for the whole country and for each of the 47 prefectures. It was published on Zenodo on 1 December 2025 (version 0.9) by Keisuke Utsu of Tokai University, from the Geospatial Information Authority of Japan (GSI) hazard information tiles and census mesh data, with Japanese documentation. Hazards integrated into one standardised table are flood, storm surge (high tide), tsunami, building-collapse zones and landslides, given as hazard levels and pixel-based ratios so they can be joined to other census mesh data; exposure files give total population and population aged over 65. Coverage: all of Japan. Access: national CSVs of about 89 to 121 MB and prefecture ZIPs on Zenodo. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free, with GSI source terms. Caveats: an aggregated estimate from zoom-level-15 hazard tiles, meant for overview-level analysis. Simulation uses: municipal hazard exposure, elderly vulnerability and evacuation planning. Related records: the Noto 2024 damage reconnaissance data.
